summary: Evidence binder for EU cross-border adequacy and ordered audit stream with legal-hold manifest
description: Issue summary: NordicBank is preparing a regulatory submission and requests a packaged evidence binder proving that Redwood audit events for their tenant preserve ordering, tamper-evidence, and comply with EU-to-US data transfer requirements. Impact: customer cannot complete regulator readiness review without artifacts (signed manifests, chain-of-custody, and data residency mapping). Customer asks: 1) A chronologically ordered audit export (delta feed) for tenant nordicbank-01 covering 2025-11-01 to 2026-02-28 with per-file RFC3161 timestamps and HMAC chain of custody. 2) A cross-border dataflow attestation listing where payloads transit (EU ingress endpoints, any US processing steps) and any subprocessors. 3) A short answers security questionnaire mapping audit fields to SOC2 control IDs and retention windows. 4) Ingest-ready sample mapping for the customer's ELK stack (Logstash templates + index mapping) and an example verification script that validates monotonic sequence IDs and checksum continuity.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - this is an evidence request rather than a bug. Suggested verification steps for internal runbook: 1) Identify tenant export bucket and time window. 2) Generate signed manifest (SHA256 per file + RFC3161 timestamp + signer key id). 3) Produce a continuity file that contains last-seen sequence ID and HMAC chain root. 4) Run validation script against exported objects to assert sequence monotonicity and checksum matches. 5) Compile cross-border flow diagram and subprocessors list for attestation.

comments: 2026-03-01 Priya Kapoor: Customer submitted an evidence request via secure form and attached the regulator's template. They marked this as time-sensitive; target submission window is 2026-03-09.
2026-03-01 Mateo Rivera: Acknowledged. I will pull export metadata and check our RFC3161 timestamping support; assigning to security-exports queue for manifest generation.

2026-03-02 Elena Novak (Exports Eng): Preliminary inventory shows tenant exports stored in s3://redwood-exports/eu/nordicbank-01/. We have per-object upload timestamps but need to generate RFC3161 timestamps retroactively for objects older than 30 days.

2026-03-03 LegalOps (via comment): Customer specifically requests a subprocessor disclosure covering any US-based analytics jobs that touch derived telemetry — please include any managed services used for indexing or monitoring.

2026-03-04 Mateo Rivera: Generated draft signed-manifest (attached). Also attached a short mapping doc for ELK ingest (Logstash pipeline + field mapping). Need Security sign-off on attestation language before sending to customer.
2026-03-05 Priya Kapoor: Customer confirmed receipt of drafts and asked for an extra line in attestation: whether exported logs include IP addresses or if IPs are redacted/pseudonymized by default.
investigation_notes: Exports Eng checked s3 inventory and found ordered-delivery keys follow 'tenant/sequence' naming. Export job writes in micro-batches which may cause small out-of-order writes when retries occur — need to reconstruct canonical order using sequence IDs stored in object metadata.

RFC3161: Our timestamp authority (TSA) was used for on-the-fly pinning after 2026-01-15; prior objects require bulk notarization by re-hashing and submitting to TSA, which will produce a notarization bundle (delay expected).

Dataflow: Ingress path for EU tenants stays within eu-west; however, analytics indexing jobs run in a separate analytics account in us-east for aggregated telemetry (per security architecture). Must disclose as subprocessors and provide minimization rationale.

Validation: Wrote a Python script prototype that iterates exports, verifies SHA256 matches manifest, checks sequence monotonicity, validates HMAC chain with customer-shared key (will request secure key exchange), and emits a short verification report.
resolution_summary: Work in progress. Deliverables produced: 1) Draft signed manifest for requested window (attached) with per-file SHA256 and signer key id. 2) ELK ingestion mapping and a validation script prototype. Outstanding items: bulk RFC3161 notarization for items before 2026-01-15 (exports team to submit notarization batch), final attestation language sign-off from Legal/Security, and confirmation from customer whether IP pseudonymization is required. Plan: complete notarization by 2026-03-08 and deliver final evidence binder (zip + manifest + verification report + Q&A mapping) to customer by 2026-03-09.
